text:
Sunset is at 4:26, and with this gray lid of cloud overhead you won't really see it, just the daylight fading a little after 4. The showers are still in town, a mix of rain and wet snow flakes, heaviest through about 8 and tapering off by 10 or 11 tonight. We're only talking a tenth to a quarter inch of water, and nothing sticks around here, though a few flakes may flit through when a heavier shower passes. It stays damp and chilly, with temperatures sliding to around 33 by morning.

Sunday starts cloudy with a stray sprinkle or flurry possible until about 9, then it turns dry. The highs top out near 43. One of the models holds onto showers longer, but I'd bet on a mostly dry day, so the umbrella can stay home if you leave after breakfast. A jacket is still a must.

The good news is that Monday is the last cool day, then the week turns sunny and mild.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-14T18:54:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Rain and snow showers will continue across the region this afternoon and evening, especially in the favored upslope locations. Showers will taper off through the day tomorrow.
  2. A warm, dry and mostly sunny week is in store.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 153 PM EST Saturday... No significant changes have been made to the forecast.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Cyclonic northwest flow will continue as the region remains under the influence of an upper level low this weekend. An embedded shortwave will pass through the region, bringing more widespread shower activity this afternoon into the evening. It's been a mix of rain and snow across the region today, with snow mostly confined to the high terrain and portions of the Northeast Kingdom this afternoon and rain most other locations. Although most locations are above freezing, temperatures may drop significantly within some of the showers, allowing for a rain/snow mix or even a brief period of snow at lower elevations. The widespread shower activity will end tonight, with lingering showers tapering off through the day tomorrow. Total snowfall accumulations this weekend look to generally be in the 1-4 inch range for locations above 2000 ft, with little to no accumulation expected at lower elevations. Temperatures will continue to remain on the cooler side this weekend, with daytime highs only climbing into the 30s to lower 40s. KEY MESSAGE 2: Unimpactful weather is expected all of the way through the upcoming week into next weekend. Following one last seasonably cool day on Monday, temperatures should be near to around 10 degrees above normal for the remainder of the period. In fact, our large scale pattern strongly favors above normal temperatures to continue for much of the following week, as well. This week does not look particularly unseasonable, however. There is only a weak signal for unusually high daytime temperatures on Wednesday and Thursday, particularly in the Champlain and Lower Connecticut River valleys, ahead of a likely cold front. Said front is currently favored to track through with little fanfare Friday morning; eventually PoPs will probably increase when timing of this boundary becomes more clear; many ensemble and deterministic models show a period of some light precipitation associated with the feature. This will be the primary exception to a period of otherwise fair weather, with ridging re-establishing itself at the start of next weekend.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Additional mountain snow is likely today as a compact system moves into our region from Canada. The valleys will have mainly showers and the mountains will have snow showers. Highs will be in the upper 30s to low 40s. This activity will taper to mountain flurries overnight. For Sunday, only scattered valley sprinkles and mountain flurries are expected with minimal accumulation. Total accumulation for this event will be little to nothing in the valleys, and 1 to 3 inches in the mountains, though isolated amounts of 4 to 5 inches can’t be ruled out at the summits. Most of this will occur today. Some higher-elevation roads may become slippery, but impacts will be minor. Next week will have a return to dry weather along with warmer temperatures, so any snow that falls or has fallen will melt. Monday will be partly sunny with highs in the 40s. Lows will be in the 20s to low 30s. Tuesday through Thursday will have plenty of sunshine. Highs will be in the 40s on Tuesday, then some 50s are likely for Wednesday and especially Thursday. With mainly clear skies at night, lows will quickly drop into the 30s each night. Friday will be dry and a touch cooler, but still pleasant, with highs in the upper 40s to low 50s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-14T12:56:00Z — same caveat): Chilly, with valley rain and mountain snow showers Saturday — The weekend brings lots of clouds, showers and cooler than average temperatures as an upper-level low spins nearby. Saturday will feature a cloudy sky with valley rain showers and persistent mountain snow, especially in northern areas, where a couple inches add up. Highs will be near 40. Mixed showers of rain and snow linger tonight, along with a cloudy sky. It will be seasonably cold, with lows in the 20s and 30s. Sunday stays mostly cloudy and chilly, with highs in the low 40s. Expect a few lingering mixed showers in the morning, before turning drier in the afternoon. A few breaks of sun are likely, especially in southern Vermont. Clouds will be stubborn on Monday, though a few late-day breaks of sun are likely. Highs again reach the low 40s. Tuesday marks the transition toward brighter and warmer weather. Expect a mix of sun and clouds, with highs near 50. The Wednesday through Friday stretch looks beautiful, with partly sunny skies and highs reaching the mid to upper 50s. The mild and quiet pattern likely continues into the beginning of Thanksgiving week.
